From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Morales <joe@greenlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: load test inputs and acceptance criteria

Joe — thanks for the clear list. I’ve sketched a concise acceptance plan and a recommended ramp that aligns with Redwood’s benchmarking playbook. Attaching the one-page plan and a CSV with the exact request distribution we want you to exercise. The attachment names are below.

Proposed acceptance targets (baseline):
- Latency (inference endpoint / text-generation): p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 220ms for the baseline model variant at 512 tokens.
- Throughput: sustain 320 qps across the test window with <3% error rate.
- Tail: 99th percentile of end-to-end request (client->response) should be <600ms.
- Stability: no more than 2 transient spikes > 2x baseline per 30-minute window.

Recommended ramp (45 minute window total):
1) Warm-up (5m): low QPS, establish KV-cache warm state.
2) Incremental ramp (20m): step to 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% target QPS (each step 5m).
3) Sustained burn (15m): hold at 100% target.
4) Cooldown (5m): taper to 0.

Artifacts we need from your side after the run (minimum):
- aggregated latency histograms (per-minute), p50/p95/p99
- raw logs for any 5xx/latency-excursions (we'll point to times)
- sample request/response pairs (10-20) for quality verification
- high-level throughput graph (1m buckets)

Attachments: [attachment: greenlane-loadplay-plan.csv (CSV, 12KB)], [attachment: greenlane-mutual-action-plan.pdf (PDF, 45KB)]

If those targets look good, can you confirm the run window and who will own traffic generation? Also let us know whether you want Redwood to coordinate a parallel run from our side (we can run a synthetic generator to compare).

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Morales <joe@greenlane.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: load test inputs and acceptance criteria — run results and next steps

Team — summary from today’s run (run-id GL-20261124-01). I’m sending an interim readout; full artifact bundle attached.

High-level verdict: PASS (acceptance criteria met with minor observations).

Key metrics (sustained 15m burn at target 320 qps):
- Sustained throughput: 318 qps average (target 320)
- Error rate: 1.1% (errors were transient 502s during a single 90s window)
- Latency: p50 = 54ms, p95 = 205ms, p99 = 410ms
- Tail behavior: three spikes above 2x baseline; two are attributable to a GC pause on the customer side (we marked these in the logs), one is a Redis cache eviction that we saw in Redwood traces.

Artifacts attached: [attachment: greenlane-results-20261118.zip (ZIP, 2.4MB)] — contains histograms CSV, raw logs (gz), sample JSONL. Also uploaded to drive and tagged GL-20261124-01.

Acceptance decision rationale: overall latency and error rates are within the thresholds defined in the loadplay plan. The Redis eviction and the short 502 window are actionable items but do not block acceptance. We recommend the following next steps: 
1) Greenlane: review the flagged 90s window and confirm mitigation plan for upstream infra (GC / connection pooling).
2) Redwood: we’ll patch the route fallback to reduce the impact of transient Redis misses — small config push scheduled for 11/26.
3) Jointly schedule a 30m production-like run after fixes (proposed 11/30).

If Greenlane agrees, we’ll mark this onboarding gate as "accepted" and move to production activation steps (token issuance, routing policies, and expected ramp schedule).

Thanks everyone — good collaboration. I’ll open a short post-run Jira (GL-ACCEPT-129) for the two action items.

—Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
